ef0ac219f3e14b73.summary: GQ India unpacks sleep medicine research on how evening alcohol consumption destroys REM sleep, suppresses growth hormone, and raises resting heart rate. Hook: 'A nightcap helps you fall asleep faster, but completely sabotages your recovery. Here is what alcohol does to your sleep stages.'
ef0ac219f3e14b73.notes:
- Sleep lab metrics: Alcohol increases initial slow-wave sleep but causes rebound fragmentation and 80% drop in second-half REM sleep
- Elevates nocturnal resting heart rate by 8-15 bpm and tanks HRV
- Suppresses natural overnight human growth hormone (HGH) pulse by up to 70%
- Practical rules: Cut off alcohol 3-4 hours before bedtime and hydrate with electrolytes
